Dec. 16 - Caramel secrets:
- Put 1/2 cup sugar plus 1 tbsp water in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Add 1/8 tsp cream of tartar along with the sugar.
- Twirl as soon as the sugar starts melting and continue until all the dry sugar is dissolved or melted. Take care not to burn it during this step; browning happens after the sugar has melted/dissolved.
- When the solution starts to become reddish, turn down the flame and move the pan off the heat.
- Add 1/4 cup warm water to the pan. It will solidify on the bottom; put the pan back on the heat and swirl the liquid to dissolve/release the hardened caramel.
- Take care not to brown it too much. Take the pan off the heat and pour the liquid caramel into a heatproof container (mason jar or glass measuring cup).

ingredients.rawText: 153 grams all-purpose flour (1 cup plus 1 tablespoon and 2 teaspoons)

instructions.text: Combine both flours and the salt in a large mixing bowl.

Knead the rested dough for another 3 minutes, then divide into two equal balls. Place on a floured surface, cover with a damp cloth, and let rise 3-4 hours at room temperature, or 8-24 hours in the refrigerator (bring refrigerated dough back to room temperature for 30-45 minutes before shaping).
Stretch each dough ball into a round or square on a floured surface using your fingers and hands, then top and bake. Yields two 12-inch pizzas.

instructions.text: Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat, add the apples, and stir to coat; cook, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, whisk together the spices, salt, and 3/4 cup sugar, then stir into the apples. Lower the heat and cook until the apples start to soften, about 5-7 minutes.

Sprinkle the flour and cornstarch over the apples and cook 3-5 minutes more. Remove from heat, stir in the cider vinegar, and scrape into a bowl to cool completely (spreading it on a rimmed baking sheet cools it faster).
Put a large baking sheet on the middle oven rack and preheat to 425°F. Roll one dough disc out on a floured surface into a roughly 12-inch round.
Fit that crust into a 9-inch pie plate leaving a 1/2-inch overhang, then freeze it. Roll the second dough disc into a 10-11 inch round.
Remove the chilled crust from the freezer, add the cooled apple filling, and cover with the second round of dough.
Press the edges together, trim the excess, crimp with a fork, and cut a few steam vents in the top crust.
Brush the top with the beaten egg and sprinkle with the remaining tablespoon of sugar.

Bake on the hot baking sheet at 425°F for 20 minutes, then lower the oven to 375°F and continue baking 30-40 minutes more, until bubbling and golden brown. Cool on a rack about 2 hours before slicing.

instructions.text: Heat oven to 350°F. Line a 9-by-13-inch cake pan with foil, overhanging the sides, and grease lightly with softened butter.

Press the remaining crust mixture evenly into the bottom of the pan and about 1/2 inch up the sides.
Bake the crust until golden and dry to the touch, 20-25 minutes. Cool on a rack, then raise the oven temperature to 375°F.

Cool completely (spreading on a parchment-lined sheet pan speeds this up).
Spread the cooled apple filling evenly over the baked crust, pressing gently to close any gaps. Break the reserved walnut topping into pebble-sized pieces and scatter or arrange over the filling.
Bake until the topping is golden brown, 45-50 minutes. Cool completely in the pan on a rack, then lift out using the foil, slide off, and cut into 24 bars (6 strips one way, 4 the other).

instructions.text: Remove the oven racks and set a baking sheet directly on the oven floor. Heat oven to 400°F. Generously butter a 1 1/2-quart soufflé dish, then coat the bottom and sides with sugar and tap out the excess, making sure sugar covers all the buttered surface for the best rise.

instructions.text: Whisk the flour, salt and baking powder together in a bowl and set aside. Coat a small loaf pan with cooking spray, then line it with plastic wrap, tucking it into the corners with plenty of overhang.

In a stand mixer with the paddle attachment, cream the butter and confectioners' sugar on medium-high until fluffy, 2-3 minutes. Add the egg and vanilla and beat on medium-high until combined, about 2 minutes, scraping the bowl as needed.
Add the flour mixture and beat on low until combined, then increase to medium and beat until the dough starts to clump together.

Turn the dough out, knead lightly, and form into a log. Cut into two pieces, one about 1/3 and the other about 2/3 of the dough. Beat the plain tahini into the larger piece until fully combined and set aside. Beat the black tahini into the smaller piece until fully combined.

On a well-floured surface, cut the white dough in half and pat half into a 5-inch square. Cut the black dough in half and pat half on top to match. Repeat with the remaining dough so you have four alternating layers. Cut in half crosswise, gently knead and roll each half to marble the colors together, then stack and briefly knead the two pieces into one soft dough.

Press the dough into the prepared loaf pan and fold the plastic wrap over the top to seal, pressing to even out the surface. Chill until firm — preferably overnight, or at least a few hours (up to 3 days ahead, or freeze up to 3 months).

Heat the oven to 325°F. Beat the egg white with 1 teaspoon water. Spread the sanding sugar on a small baking sheet. Unmold the dough, trim the sides square if desired, lightly brush the outside with the egg white mixture, then roll and press it in the sugar to coat all sides except the ends.
Cut the block into barely 1/4-inch-thick slices and lay them 1 inch apart on parchment- or silicone-mat-lined baking sheets. Freeze until firm, about 10 minutes.
Bake until golden underneath, 14-16 minutes. Cool a few minutes on the sheets, then transfer to wire racks to cool completely. Keeps in an airtight container at room temperature up to 1 week.

instructions.text: Combine the mirin and sake in a small saucepan and bring to a boil over high heat. Boil 20 seconds without boiling off too much liquid, then lower the heat and whisk in the miso and sugar, stirring over medium heat until the sugar dissolves (don't let it boil). Remove from heat and whisk in the sesame oil, then let cool and transfer to a wide glass, stainless steel bowl, or baking dish.
Pat the fish fillets dry, brush or rub with the marinade on both sides, and place in the dish, turning a few times to coat. Cover and marinate 2-3 hours, or up to a day.
Light the broiler or prepare a grill. Line a sheet pan with oiled foil. Tap each fillet against the dish to let excess marinade drip off; place skin side up on the sheet pan if broiling.

Grill skin side down, or broil skin side up, about 6 inches from the heat, 2-3 minutes per side until browned and blackened in spots. If needed, finish in a 400°F oven about 5 minutes more, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.

instructions.text: In a small saucepan over high heat, boil the sugar with 1 cup (240 ml) water, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Reduce to a simmer, add the lemon juice and extract, and simmer until thickened into a syrup, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool.
Heat the oven to 400°F. Butter a 9-by-13-inch baking dish. In a large bowl, stir together the semolina, melted butter and sugar until well combined; set aside.
Stir the yogurt and baking soda together in a bowl and let sit until it nearly doubles in size, about 10 minutes.

Pour the yogurt mixture over the semolina mixture and mix well. Transfer to the buttered dish and press into an even layer. Score the surface on the diagonal into 2-inch diamonds and top each diamond with an almond. Bake until golden brown, 25-30 minutes.
Set the dish on a wire rack and drizzle the cooled syrup over the hot cake. Let cool to room temperature before recutting along the scored lines and serving.

instructions.text: In a food processor, pulse the flour and salt together. Add the butter and pulse until the mixture forms lima-bean-size pieces. Slowly add the ice water, 1 tablespoon at a time, pulsing until the dough just comes together — it should be moist but not wet.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface, gather into a ball, and flatten into a disk with the heel of your hand. Wrap tightly in plastic and refrigerate at least 1 hour and up to 2 days.

instructions.text: Heat the oven to 375°F. Put the cauliflower in a large bowl, pour on enough olive oil to coat (a few tablespoons), season generously with salt and pepper, and toss gently until evenly coated.

Spread the cauliflower on a baking sheet and drizzle any remaining oil from the bowl on top. Bake, turning once, until caramelized at the edges and tender, 25-30 minutes. Serve warm or at room temperature as a side dish; a splash of good aged vinegar is nice on top.

Cook on low until the chicken is tender and the flavors meld, 5-6 hours. (If you'll be away 8+ hours, set the cook time to 4 hours on low and let the auto-switch to warm handle the rest.)

Shred the chicken coarsely with two forks. With the heat still on low, stir in the scallions and cilantro. Season to taste with salt and lime juice, then serve with rice or in tortillas with your choice of accompaniments.

instructions.text: Combine the yogurt, cucumbers, chopped mint and garlic in a medium bowl and mix well. Chill until ready to serve.
In a second bowl, mix the beef, onion, turmeric, 1 teaspoon of the salt and plenty of black pepper until well combined.

Heat a large well-seasoned cast-iron skillet (or other heavy-bottomed pan) over medium-high. Once very hot, break the beef into large, irregular chunks with two spoons or your hands and drop into the skillet. Cook undisturbed until charred and crisp on the bottom and browned partway up the sides, 6-8 minutes.

With a wooden spoon, toss the meat and break up any large pieces. Add the walnuts and raisins and continue cooking, stirring often, until the meat reaches your desired doneness and the walnuts are toasted, 2-3 minutes more.

Take the yogurt from the fridge and season with the remaining teaspoon of salt. Spread it on a serving platter, top with the crispy meat, drizzle with pomegranate molasses if using, and garnish with mint leaves. Serve with warmed pita or rice.

instructions.text: Combine 2 teaspoons ground cumin, the chile powder and 1 teaspoon salt. Cut shallow crosshatched incisions across the top and bottom of the steak, then rub the spice mix all over it (gloves recommended, the chile powder is hot). Place the steak in a resealable freezer bag.

Whisk together the lime juice and zest, 1/4 cup olive oil, the Worcestershire sauce and half the garlic. Reserve 2 tablespoons of this marinade and pour the rest into the bag with the steak. Seal, coat thoroughly, place on a sheet pan and refrigerate at least 4 hours and up to 24, massaging the bag occasionally. Refrigerate the reserved marinade too if cooking the next day.

Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large, heavy skillet over medium-high. Add the onion and cook, stirring, until softened and starting to color, 4-5 minutes. Stir in the bell peppers and chile and cook, stirring, until the peppers begin to soften, about 3 minutes.
Lower the heat to medium, add the remaining garlic and cumin, and salt to taste. Cook, stirring often, until the peppers are nicely seared, softened and starting to caramelize, 5-8 minutes.
Pour in the reserved 2 tablespoons of marinade and scrape up the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon. Stir in half the cilantro, taste and adjust seasoning, then remove from heat but keep warm.
Wrap the tortillas in foil and warm in a low oven, or wrap in a towel and warm in a steamer or the microwave.

Heat a large cast-iron skillet over medium-high, or prepare a medium-hot grill. Remove the steak from the marinade (discard the marinade) and pat dry. If using a skillet, heat the remaining tablespoon of oil (cut the steak in half and cook in batches if it doesn't fit). Cook 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Rest on a cutting board, tented with foil, for 10 minutes, then slice across the grain into 1/2- to 3/4-inch strips.

Arrange the lettuce on a platter and place the sliced steak next to it. Pour any accumulated juices from the cutting board over the meat and sprinkle with the remaining cilantro. Serve the vegetables on the same platter or separately, along with warm tortillas, salsa and crumbled queso fresco.

instructions.text: Heat the broiler. Warm the olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed soup pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. After 2 minutes, stir the mussels, replace the lid, and continue cooking until all the mussels have opened, 6-8 minutes.
Brush the cut sides of the baguette pieces with oil and toast cut-side up under the broiler. Rub the toasts with the remaining garlic cloves.
Stir the chopped parsley into the mussels, then ladle the mussels and broth into bowls. Serve with the garlic toasts.

instructions.text: Butter a 13-by-9-inch baking pan and line with buttered parchment paper. Preheat the oven to 350°F. Melt the butter, chocolate and both sugars together in a double boiler over barely simmering water, or in a microwave on low power, and let cool slightly. In a large bowl or mixer, whisk the eggs, then whisk in the salt and vanilla.

Whisk the chocolate mixture into the eggs. Fold in the flour just until combined, then stir in the chopped walnuts if using. Pour the batter into the prepared pan; if using whole walnuts, arrange them on top of the batter. Bake 35-40 minutes, until shiny and beginning to crack on top. Cool in the pan on a rack.

instructions.text: Heat the oven to 350°F with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Coat a 9-by-13-inch pan with nonstick spray and line with parchment, leaving 2 inches of excess on the long sides to help lift the blondies out later.

If using whole graham crackers, pulse them in a food processor (or crush in a bag with a rolling pin) into a fine powder. Add the flour, baking powder and salt to the crumbs and pulse a few times to combine.

In a stand mixer with the paddle attachment, cream the butter, brown sugar and granulated sugar on medium until light and fluffy, 4-5 minutes. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing well after each and scraping the bowl.

Mix in the vanilla. On low speed, add the graham crumb mixture and mix just to combine. Mix in about 3/4 of the chocolate. Transfer the dough to the prepared pan and press into an even layer with damp hands.

Bake on the lower rack until golden at the edges with a crackly surface, 30-32 minutes. Remove from the oven, sprinkle the marshmallows evenly over the top, and return to the upper rack. Bake until the marshmallows soften and turn golden brown, 6-8 minutes.

Remove the pan. If any marshmallows have puffed up, pop them with a toothpick or skewer (they deflate easily). Sprinkle the reserved chocolate over the top and return to the upper rack; bake until the chocolate is melted and the marshmallows lightly toasted, about 2 minutes. Cool on a rack for 45 minutes.
Run a thin knife between the blondies and the pan on the short sides, then lift out using the parchment sling. Cool 10 more minutes, then slice into 12 pieces and serve.
